subproblem.title: Vague convergence gives convergence of ball measures at μ-null spheres (Simon 7.3.1 proof, display (4))
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (ρ : ℝ), 0 < ρ → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → μ (ball 0 r) ≠ ∞) → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → ∀ᶠ j in atTop, μs j (ball 0 r) ≠ ∞) → (∀ f : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous f → HasCompactSupport f → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ y, f y ∂(μs j)) atTop (𝓝 (∫ y, f y ∂μ))) → μ (sphere 0 ρ) = 0 → Tendsto (fun j => μs j (ball 0 ρ)) atTop (𝓝 (μ (ball 0 ρ)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon 7.3.1 proof, display (4) (chapter-07.txt lines 348–351). The compact sets F of the parent's step 3(i) are taken to be closed balls, so inner regularity is replaced by continuity from below. Hypotheses in the order of the Lean statement: (H1) ρ > 0; (H2) μ(B_r(0)) ≠ ∞ for every r > 0; (H3) for every r > 0, μ_j(B_r(0)) ≠ ∞ for all sufficiently large j; (H4) ∫f dμ_j → ∫f dμ for every continuous compactly supported f : ℝ^P → ℝ; (H5) μ(sphere(0, ρ)) = 0. All measures live on the Borel sets of ℝ^P. ofReal : ℝ → [0, ∞] is continuous and monotone. ∫ denotes the Bochner integral, which is 0 for non-integrable functions.
1. Cut-off functions. For real a < b let φ_{a,b}(y) := min(1, max(0, (b − |y|)/(b − a))). It is continuous and 0 ≤ φ_{a,b} ≤ 1. Also φ_{a,b}(y) = 1 if |y| ≤ a (then (b − |y|)/(b − a) ≥ 1), and φ_{a,b}(y) = 0 if |y| ≥ b. Hence support φ_{a,b} ⊆ B_b(0) and tsupport φ_{a,b} ⊆ closedBall(0, b), which is compact because ℝ^P is proper. So φ_{a,b} is continuous with compact support.
2. Integral comparisons. Let ν be any measure on ℝ^P, let a < b with b > 0, and put φ := φ_{a,b}.
 (i) ofReal(∫φ dν) ≤ ν(B_b(0)). Since φ ≥ 0 is measurable, ∫φ dν = (∫⁻ ofReal(φ) dν).toReal, whether or not φ is ν-integrable (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae; if the lintegral is ∞ both sides are 0). Therefore ofReal(∫φ dν) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(φ) dν, using ofReal(t.toReal) ≤ t. Since ofReal(φ) ≤ 1_{B_b(0)} pointwise, ∫⁻ ofReal(φ) dν ≤ ν(B_b(0)).
 (ii) If ν(B_b(0)) < ∞, then ν(E) ≤ ofReal(∫φ dν) for every measurable E on which φ = 1. Indeed, 1_E ≤ ofReal(φ) pointwise gives ν(E) ≤ ∫⁻ ofReal(φ) dν ≤ ν(B_b(0)) < ∞. As this lintegral is finite, ofReal((∫⁻ ofReal(φ) dν).toReal) = ∫⁻ ofReal(φ) dν, and the formula in (i) gives the claim.
3. Lower bound: μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(B_ρ(0)). Fix k ∈ ℕ, put a_k := ρ − 1/(k+1) < ρ and φ := φ_{a_k, ρ}.
- By (H4), ∫φ dμ_j → ∫φ dμ, hence ofReal(∫φ dμ_j) → ofReal(∫φ dμ).
- By 2(i) (ν = μ_j, b = ρ), ofReal(∫φ dμ_j) ≤ μ_j(B_ρ(0)) for every j. So ofReal(∫φ dμ) = lim_j ofReal(∫φ dμ_j) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(B_ρ(0)).
- By 2(ii) (ν = μ, with μ(B_ρ(0)) < ∞ by (H1)–(H2), and E = closedBall(0, a_k)), μ(closedBall(0, a_k)) ≤ ofReal(∫φ dμ) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(B_ρ(0)).
The closed balls closedBall(0, a_k) increase in k and their union is B_ρ(0): a_k < ρ, and |y| < ρ implies |y| ≤ a_k for large k. By continuity of measure from below, μ(B_ρ(0)) = sup_k μ(closedBall(0, a_k)) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(B_ρ(0)).
4. Upper bound: limsup_j μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ)) ≤ μ(closedBall(0, ρ)). Fix k ∈ ℕ, put b_k := ρ + 1/(k+1) and g := φ_{ρ, b_k}, so g = 1 on closedBall(0, ρ) and g = 0 outside B_{b_k}(0).
- By (H3) there is j_0 with μ_j(B_{b_k}(0)) < ∞ for all j ≥ j_0. For such j, 2(ii) (ν = μ_j, E = closedBall(0, ρ)) gives μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ)) ≤ ofReal(∫g dμ_j).
- By (H4), ofReal(∫g dμ_j) → ofReal(∫g dμ). Hence limsup_j μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ)) ≤ ofReal(∫g dμ), and ofReal(∫g dμ) ≤ μ(B_{b_k}(0)) by 2(i) (ν = μ).
The open balls B_{b_k}(0) decrease in k and their intersection is closedBall(0, ρ). Also μ(B_{b_0}(0)) = μ(B_{ρ+1}(0)) < ∞ by (H2). By continuity of measure from above, inf_k μ(B_{b_k}(0)) = μ(closedBall(0, ρ)). Hence limsup_j μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ)) ≤ μ(closedBall(0, ρ)).
5. Null boundary. closedBall(0, ρ) = B_ρ(0) ∪ sphere(0, ρ). By subadditivity and (H5), μ(closedBall(0, ρ)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(0)) + μ(sphere(0, ρ)) = μ(B_ρ(0)).
6. Conclusion. Since μ_j(B_ρ(0)) ≤ μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ)), steps 4, 5 and 3 give limsup_j μ_j(B_ρ(0)) ≤ limsup_j μ_j(closedBall(0, ρ)) ≤ μ(closedBall(0, ρ)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ liminf_j μ_j(B_ρ(0)). In the complete linear order [0, ∞] with its order topology, liminf ≥ L ≥ limsup implies convergence to L (tendsto_of_le_liminf_of_limsup_le; the boundedness side conditions are automatic in [0, ∞]). Hence μ_j(B_ρ(0)) → μ(B_ρ(0)). This is the portmanteau sandwich; Mathlib's Portmanteau file is not imported by GMT.Ch07.Submission, so the sandwich is carried out directly as above.
proof_key_steps: Radial piecewise-linear cut-offs φ_{a,b} are continuous with compact support, 0 ≤ φ ≤ 1, equal to 1 on closedBall(0,a) and 0 off B_b(0).
ofReal(∫φ dν) ≤ ν(B_b(0)) for every ν, and ν(E) ≤ ofReal(∫φ dν) when ν(B_b(0)) < ∞ and φ = 1 on E (via ∫φ = (∫⁻ ofReal φ).toReal).
Lower bound μ(B_ρ(0)) ≤ liminf μ_j(B_ρ(0)), via φ_{ρ−1/(k+1), ρ} and continuity from below over closed balls.
Upper bound limsup μ_j(closedBall(0,ρ)) ≤ μ(closedBall(0,ρ)), via φ_{ρ, ρ+1/(k+1)}, eventual finiteness of μ_j on balls, and continuity from above.
The null sphere gives μ(closedBall(0,ρ)) ≤ μ(B_ρ(0)); the liminf/limsup sandwich in [0, ∞] gives convergence.

audit.reason: The type exactly expresses the stated finiteness, test-function convergence and null-sphere hypotheses. The explicit cutoffs and integral comparisons correctly handle non-integrable Bochner integrals. Eventual finiteness is used precisely for the upper comparison; limit-measure finiteness justifies continuity from above. Increasing closed balls give the lower bound, and the null sphere closes the liminf/limsup sandwich. The proof is complete and independent.

subproblem.title: Ball-measure identity extends from μ-null-sphere radii to all radii (Simon 7.3.1 proof, after display (4))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on the Borel sets of ℝ^P (Measure (Euclid P)) with μ(B_r(0)) < ∞ for every r > 0, and let c ∈ [0, ∞] with c ≠ ∞. Suppose μ(B_ρ(0)) = c·ofReal(ρⁿ) for every ρ > 0 such that μ(sphere(0, ρ)) = 0, where sphere(0, ρ) = {y : |y| = ρ}. Then μ(B_ρ(0)) = c·ofReal(ρⁿ) for every ρ > 0.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (c : ℝ≥0∞), c ≠ ∞ → (∀ r : ℝ, 0 < r → μ (ball 0 r) ≠ ∞) → (∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → μ (sphere 0 ρ) = 0 → μ (ball 0 ρ) = c * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)) → ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → μ (ball 0 ρ) = c * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon 7.3.1 proof after display (4). The book says μ_C(∂B_ρ(0)) = 0 "is true except for at most a countable set of ρ", and the identity is then asserted "for each ρ > 0" (chapter-07.txt lines 348–355). Hypotheses in the order of the Lean statement: (H1) c ≠ ∞; (H2) μ(B_r(0)) ≠ ∞ for every r > 0; (H3) μ(B_ρ(0)) = c·ofReal(ρⁿ) for every ρ > 0 with μ(sphere(0, ρ)) = 0. Call t ∈ ℝ bad if μ(sphere(0, t)) > 0, and let N be the set of bad t. By (H3), μ(B_r(0)) = c·ofReal(rⁿ) for every r > 0 with r ∉ N.
1. N is countable. For m ∈ ℕ let ν_m := μ⌞B_{m+1}(0) (μ.restrict (ball 0 (m+1))). It is a finite measure, since ν_m(ℝ^P) = μ(B_{m+1}(0)) < ∞ by (H2). The spheres sphere(0, t) = {y : |y| = t}, t ∈ ℝ, are the level sets of the measurable map y ↦ |y|, so they are pairwise disjoint measurable sets. In the finite measure space (ℝ^P, ν_m) at most countably many of them have positive measure: for each k ≥ 1, at most k·ν_m(ℝ^P) of them have measure ≥ 1/k (Mathlib: Measure.countable_meas_level_set_pos applied to the norm, or countable_meas_pos_of_disjoint_of_meas_iUnion_ne_top). So N_m := {t : ν_m(sphere(0, t)) > 0} is countable. Now let t ∈ N. Then t ≥ 0, since for t < 0 the sphere is empty. Choose m ∈ ℕ with t < m + 1. Then sphere(0, t) ⊆ B_{m+1}(0), so ν_m(sphere(0, t)) = μ(sphere(0, t)) > 0 and t ∈ N_m. Hence N ⊆ ⋃_m N_m is countable.
2. Every nonempty open interval (a, b) ⊆ ℝ contains a point not in N. A countable subset of ℝ is Lebesgue-null (Set.Countable.measure_zero), whereas volume((a, b)) = b − a > 0 (Real.volume_Ioo); so (a, b) ⊄ N.
3. Fix ρ > 0. For k ∈ ℕ put s_k := ρ − ρ/(k+1). Then 0 ≤ s_k < ρ, (s_k) is increasing, and s_k → ρ. By step 2 choose r_k ∈ (s_k, ρ) with r_k ∉ N. Then 0 < r_k < ρ, μ(B_{r_k}(0)) = c·ofReal(r_kⁿ) by (H3), and r_k → ρ (squeezed between s_k and ρ).
4. Lower bound. B_{r_k}(0) ⊆ B_ρ(0) gives c·ofReal(r_kⁿ) ≤ μ(B_ρ(0)) for all k. Since t ↦ ofReal(tⁿ) is continuous, ofReal(r_kⁿ) → ofReal(ρⁿ). Since c ≠ ∞ (H1), multiplication by c is continuous there (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul), so c·ofReal(r_kⁿ) → c·ofReal(ρⁿ). Limits preserve the non-strict inequality, so c·ofReal(ρⁿ) ≤ μ(B_ρ(0)).
5. Upper bound. Since s_k < r_k, μ(B_{s_k}(0)) ≤ μ(B_{r_k}(0)) = c·ofReal(r_kⁿ) ≤ c·ofReal(ρⁿ). The last inequality uses 0 < r_k ≤ ρ and monotonicity of t ↦ tⁿ on [0, ∞), of ofReal, and of multiplication by c. The balls B_{s_k}(0) increase, and their union is B_ρ(0): s_k < ρ, and |y| < ρ implies |y| < s_k for large k because s_k → ρ. By continuity of measure from below, μ(B_ρ(0)) = lim_k μ(B_{s_k}(0)) ≤ c·ofReal(ρⁿ).
6. Steps 4 and 5 give μ(B_ρ(0)) = c·ofReal(ρⁿ).
proof_key_steps: The set N of radii t with μ(sphere(0,t)) > 0 is countable: restrict μ to B_{m+1}(0), a finite measure, whose disjoint norm level sets are the spheres.
Every open interval meets ℝ \ N, because countable sets are Lebesgue-null and intervals are not.
Choose radii r_k ∈ (ρ − ρ/(k+1), ρ) outside N, so r_k → ρ⁻ and μ(B_{r_k}(0)) = c·ofReal(r_kⁿ).
Lower bound: c·ofReal(r_kⁿ) ≤ μ(B_ρ(0)), then pass to the limit using c ≠ ∞.
Upper bound: μ(B_{s_k}(0)) ≤ c·ofReal(ρⁿ), then continuity from below as s_k ↑ ρ.

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean proposition agree, including arbitrary natural dimensions and finite ENNReal coefficient. Finite restrictions establish countability of charged spheres, and Lebesgue-nullness supplies good radii in every interval. The proof correctly separates the possibly nonmonotone good radii from the monotone auxiliary radii used for continuity from below. Both inequalities follow with all hypotheses justified and no circular reliance.

subproblem.title: Scaling limit of rescaled ball measures (Simon 7.3.1 proof, display (1))
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ. Let μ and μ_j (j ∈ ℕ) be measures on the Borel sets of ℝ^P (Measure (Euclid P)), x ∈ ℝ^P and θ ∈ ℝ. Let λ_j ∈ ℝ with λ_j > 0 for every j and λ_j → 0. Write ω_n := unitBallVolume n (the Lebesgue measure of the open unit ball of ℝⁿ), and η_j := dilation x λ_j, η_j(y) = −λ_j⁻¹x + λ_j⁻¹y. Assume (H3) μ(B_r(x)) / (ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) → ofReal θ in [0, ∞] as r → 0⁺ (filter 𝓝[>] 0, division in [0, ∞]). Assume (H4) μ_j(s) = ofReal((λ_j⁻¹)ⁿ)·μ(η_j⁻¹(s)) for every j and every measurable s ⊆ ℝ^P. Then for every ρ > 0, μ_j(B_ρ(0)) → ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)·ofReal θ in [0, ∞] as j → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (μs : ℕ → Measure (Euclid P)) (x : Euclid P) (θ : ℝ) (lams : ℕ → ℝ), (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → Tendsto (fun r : ℝ => μ (ball x r) / (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (r ^ n))) (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 (ENNReal.ofReal θ)) → (∀ (j : ℕ) (s : Set (Euclid P)), MeasurableSet s → μs j s = ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j)⁻¹ ^ n) * μ (dilation x (lams j) ⁻¹' s)) → ∀ ρ : ℝ, 0 < ρ → Tendsto (fun j => μs j (ball 0 ρ)) atTop (𝓝 (unitBallVolume n * ENNReal.ofReal (ρ ^ n) * ENNReal.ofReal θ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent proof, i.e. Simon 7.3.1 proof, display (1) with "for each R > 0" (chapter-07.txt lines 329–335), restated for measures. Hypotheses in the order of the Lean statement: (H1) λ_j > 0 for every j; (H2) λ_j → 0; (H3) q(r) := μ(B_r(x))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) → ofReal θ as r → 0 in the filter 𝓝[>] 0, where ω_n := unitBallVolume n and / is division in [0, ∞]; (H4) μ_j(s) = ofReal((λ_j⁻¹)ⁿ)·μ((dilation x λ_j)⁻¹(s)) for every j and every measurable s. Fix ρ > 0 and put K := ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ).
1. 0 < ω_n < ∞. ω_n is the volume of the open unit ball B_1(0) of Euclid n = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n), whose volume is an additive Haar measure. It is positive on the nonempty open set B_1(0) (Metric.measure_ball_pos) and finite on the bounded set B_1(0) (measure_ball_lt_top; Euclid n is proper). This holds for every n, including n = 0 (a one-point space, ω_0 = 1). Hence K ≠ ∞. For every r > 0, L_r := ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ) satisfies L_r ≠ 0 (as ofReal(rⁿ) > 0) and L_r ≠ ∞.
2. Preimages of balls. Let λ > 0 and y ∈ ℝ^P. By the definitions of dilation and dilationCLM, dilation x λ y = −(λ⁻¹•x) + dilationCLM P λ y = −(λ⁻¹•x) + λ⁻¹•y = λ⁻¹•(y − x). Hence |dilation x λ y| = λ⁻¹·|y − x|, and |dilation x λ y| < ρ ⟺ |y − x| < λρ (multiply by λ > 0) ⟺ dist(y, x) < λρ. Thus (dilation x λ)⁻¹(B_ρ(0)) = B_{λρ}(x).
3. Fix j. B_ρ(0) is open, hence measurable. So (H4) and step 2 (with λ = λ_j > 0 by (H1)) give μ_j(B_ρ(0)) = ofReal((λ_j⁻¹)ⁿ)·μ(B_{λ_jρ}(x)).
4. Algebra in [0, ∞]. Let λ := λ_j, r := λρ > 0 and A := μ(B_r(x)) ∈ [0, ∞]. Since a/b = a·b⁻¹ in [0, ∞], K·(A/L_r) = (K/L_r)·A for every A, including A = ∞ (ENNReal.mul_comm_div). Moreover:
- K/L_r = (ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ))/(ω_n·ofReal(rⁿ)) = ofReal(ρⁿ)/ofReal(rⁿ), cancelling the common factor ω_n ∉ {0, ∞} (ENNReal.mul_div_mul_left);
- ofReal(ρⁿ)/ofReal(rⁿ) = ofReal(ρⁿ/rⁿ), since rⁿ > 0 (ENNReal.ofReal_div_of_pos);
- ofReal(ρⁿ/rⁿ) = ofReal((λ⁻¹)ⁿ), because rⁿ = λⁿρⁿ and ρⁿ/(λⁿρⁿ) = (λ⁻¹)ⁿ for λ, ρ ≠ 0.
Combining with step 3: μ_j(B_ρ(0)) = K·q(λ_jρ) for every j.
5. By (H2), λ_jρ → 0·ρ = 0, and λ_jρ > 0 for every j by (H1). Hence λ_jρ → 0 in the filter 𝓝[>] 0 (tendsto_nhdsWithin_iff). Composing with (H3), q(λ_jρ) → ofReal θ.
6. Multiplication by the constant K ≠ ∞ is continuous on [0, ∞] (ENNReal.Tendsto.const_mul with side condition K ≠ ∞). So K·q(λ_jρ) → K·ofReal θ = ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)·ofReal θ. By step 4 the sequence μ_j(B_ρ(0)) coincides term by term with K·q(λ_jρ), so μ_j(B_ρ(0)) → ω_n·ofReal(ρⁿ)·ofReal θ.
